benchmark: UNSC-Bench, pinned vetoed row 11, linked to existing action-review-v2 cases
question: Does the existing plan-to-text adapter retain given benchmark actions and qualifications in a separate Gaza context, without inventing an Indian abstention, unanimous agreement or future UK approval?

units.description: This is the 8 December 2023 vote on draft S/2023/970 at S/PV.9499, a retrospective analysis, not a prospective forecast.
units.quote: The draft resolution received 13 votes in favour, 1 against and 1 abstention.

units.description: The recorded tally is 13 Yes, one No and one Abstain; the US cast the No vote.
units.quote: Against: United States of America Abstaining: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

units.description: The draft was not adopted because a permanent member, the US, voted against it; a large Yes majority did not mean adoption.
units.quote: The draft resolution was not adopted, owing to the negative vote of a permanent member of the Council.

units.description: France voted Yes on S/2023/970.
units.quote: That is why France voted in favour of draft resolution S/2023/970

units.description: France seeks a new immediate and lasting humanitarian truce that can lead to a permanent ceasefire.
units.quote: we are pleading for a new, immediate and lasting humanitarian truce that can lead to a permanent ceasefire.

units.description: France sees fighting terrorism and protecting civilians as compatible, under strict international humanitarian law.
units.quote: we see no contradiction between the fight against terrorism and the protection of civilians in strict compliance with international humanitarian law.

units.description: France also wanted the Council to condemn the 7 October Hamas and other terrorist-group attacks; this preference did not prevent its Yes vote.
units.quote: We would have liked to see the Council finally condemn the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other terrorist groups on 7 October.

units.description: France remains committed to mobilizing the Council on security, humanitarian and especially political aspects of the crisis.
units.quote: France will continue to be resolutely committed to the full mobilization of the Council on all aspects of the crisis

units.description: The UK recorded an Abstain, not a Yes or No vote.
units.quote: That is why we abstained in the voting on the draft resolution (S/2023/970).

units.description: The UK expressed concern about civilian deaths and displacement in Gaza.
units.quote: The scale of civilian deaths and displacement in Gaza cannot continue.

units.description: The UK welcomed the prior humanitarian pause, hostage releases and aid deliveries, and calls for further and longer pauses for aid and hostage releases.
units.quote: We call for further and longer pauses to get aid to Palestinians and allow space for further hostage releases.

units.description: The UK explains that it cannot support a draft omitting condemnation of the 7 October Hamas atrocities.
units.quote: we cannot vote in favour of a draft resolution that does not condemn the atrocities Hamas committed against innocent Israeli civilians on 7 October.

units.description: The UK argues that the ceasefire call ignores Hamas acts of terror and continuing hostage detention; attribute this rationale to the UK.
units.quote: Calling for a ceasefire ignores the fact that Hamas has committed acts of terror and is still holding civilians hostage.

units.description: The UK says Israel must be able to address the Hamas threat while abiding by international humanitarian law.
units.quote: Israel needs to be able to address the threat posed by Hamas, and it needs to do so in a manner that abides by international humanitarian law

units.description: The UK supports a two-State solution delivering Palestinian statehood, Israeli security and peace for both sides.
units.quote: a two-State solution that delivers statehood for Palestinians, security for Israel and peace for people on both sides.

units.description: Adding a Hamas-condemnation clause in an authored future draft does not by itself establish a later UK Yes vote or agreed settlement; the supplied statement does not announce that counterfactual vote.
Brazil voted Yes on the UAE/Arab-group draft S/2023/970.
units.quote: Brazil voted in favour of the draft resolution proposed by the United Arab Emirates on behalf of the Group of Arab States (S/2023/970)

units.description: Brazil also co-sponsored that draft.
units.quote: which we also co-sponsored.

units.description: Brazil advocates an immediate humanitarian ceasefire.
units.quote: the Council demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire

units.description: Brazil advocates easing humanitarian aid.
units.quote: the easing of humanitarian aid

units.description: Brazil advocates immediate and unconditional release of all hostages.
units.quote: the immediate and unconditional release of all the hostages.

units.description: Brazil warns that inaction may irreparably harm the prospect of a two-State solution.
units.quote: We might be irreparably harming the prospect of a two-State solution.

units.description: Brazil will work with Council members to restore conditions for humanitarian action in Gaza.
units.quote: Brazil will continue to work with Council members with a view to re-establishing the conditions for humanitarian action to resume in Gaza.

units.description: Brazil suggests a more effective negotiating process with draft responsibility on all Member States.
units.quote: effective negotiating process, which will place the full responsibility of a draft resolution on all Member States.

units.description: India was not a Council member for this vote and has no recorded Council vote here. Nonmembership is not a recorded Abstain.
The selected record supplies no Indian national statement; do not invent its Gaza position or imply it opposed the draft. This is bounded missing information, not a claim about all Indian policy.
France, the UK and Brazil express humanitarian concerns. Do not extend that documented common ground to India from this packet.

France and Brazil voted Yes while the UK abstained; France and the UK both wanted Hamas condemnation, showing that a shared concern does not uniquely determine the procedural vote. Preserve truce/ceasefire versus UK pause qualifications.

Any proposal to examine civilian protection, hostage release, terrorism wording and humanitarian-law compliance is an analyst suggestion, not an agreed government commitment, a new negotiation or guaranteed UK approval.
